title: Preference Optimization in Practice: RLHF, DPO, IPO, KTO, ORPO and SimPO
summary: The preference-tuning family on one map: which data each method needs, whether it learns online or offline, whether it keeps a reference model, and what that costs in GPU memory. Then hands-on DPO and IPO with LoRA, KTO for thumbs-up/down feedback, one-stage ORPO, length-normalised SimPO, and how to choose a method and check that it worked.
objectives: Place RLHF-PPO, RLOO/GRPO, DPO, IPO, KTO, ORPO, SimPO and CPO by data, online/offline, reference model and memory, and compute the model-state memory of each for an 8B model
Run DPO or IPO with LoRA in TRL, explain how the reference model comes from disabling the adapters, and read rewards/chosen, rewards/rejected, rewards/margins and rewards/accuracies
Compute the KTO, ORPO and SimPO losses for a worked example and say when each beats DPO
Choose a method from the feedback, memory and goal you have, and evaluate the result with a length-aware win rate against the SFT model
prerequisites: The theory of preference tuning from [Preference Tuning: RLHF and DPO](/learn/fine-tuning/preference-tuning), especially [the DPO derivation](/learn/fine-tuning/preference-tuning/dpo). Memory per parameter from [Start Here](/learn/fine-tuning/start-here/sizing-your-first-run). A working environment from [Run fine-tuning yourself](/learn/fine-tuning/run-fine-tuning-yourself) and an SFT model from [SFT with LoRA, step by step](/learn/fine-tuning/sft-with-lora-step-by-step).
